finding: The 'SAR 235bn ≈ 7.6% of deposits' figure. The arithmetic is 235.443/3,075.74 = 7.65%, which rounds to 7.7%, not 7.6%. More important, it overstates the drain on bank deposits. (b) The total includes an early repurchase of more than SAR 17bn that was settled in new sukuk, so no new cash was raised. (c) It includes 'government alternative funding'. finding: The direction 'slower corporate loan growth' is not supported by its own evidence. 'Slower' holds only against the 2022-25 trend (12.3% CAGR). (2) The MoF attributes the -2.1% capex change to accelerated military spending in 2026, not to civil project cuts. (3) 2027 capex of SAR 178bn is +10% on the FY2026 budget (162), general items including the mega-projects allocation rise 6%, and municipal services rise 12%.
fix: P-B-02 restated: loan growth below the 2022-25 trend but flat-to-higher vs 2026; capex change attributed per MoF to military spending brought forward; direction neutral to slightly negative, Low confidence.

fix: Privatisation and share-sale signal added (V-019; P-E-03; section 2).

fix: P-E-06 rebuilt around margins, feedstock notices and Zakat; tariff effect not quantified; utility supply marked unverified.

finding: The quantified 9M 2026 finance costs of SAR 976m vs 668m (+46%) reflect borrowings that rose to SAR 20.25bn after the Shelf Drilling acquisition. finding: Confidence High is too high and the mechanism is misstated. Under Basel III the countercyclical buffer is a CET1 buffer, so AT1 sukuk raise Tier 1 ratios but do not satisfy it (check against SAMA's CCyB rules). The SAR 34.5bn includes Al Rajhi's USD 600m Tier 2, and the source does not tie the issuance to the CCyB; Argaam's analysts list retained earnings and lower payouts as the main tools. The buffer has applied since 25 May 2026, so its incremental 2027 effect is small.
fix: P-B-06 reworded: CCyB is a CET1 buffer met via retained earnings; AT1 coupons affect ordinary-equity returns; confidence Medium.

finding: The escalation after 30 Sep 2026 is not reflected in the base case. Bank Q3 filings (BSF, SAIB, SNB, Alinma) report a significant escalation after 30 Sep.
